newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS CREDITS LATE COACH FOR FIGHTING ATTITUDE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS CREDITS LATE COACH FOR FIGHTING ATTITUDE.

text.p: Newly-crowned Australian Open champion Pete Sampras thanked his late coach and mentor Tim Gullikson on Sunday for giving him the strength and courage to lift his ninth Grand Slam title.
Sampras, 25, described his Australian Open title as the toughest major he has ever contested after surviving two five-set marathons and energy-sapping conditions to reach his 11th Grand Slam final.
Gullikson's death last year from brain tumours had a massive impact on the 25-year-old from Florida, who said on Sunday his coach was his inspiration on the tennis court.
Sampras broke down in tears two years ago at a news conference after learning of Gullikson's illness during the Open in Melbourne.
"Where it all happened was here in Australia and I thought about it I woke up today and before the match," he said after his 6-2 6-3 6-3 victory over Spain's Carlos Moya.
"I'm sure he's looking down very happy that I fought through some tough matches, because that was one thing he instilled in me was attitude, not quitting.
"That's one thing I will always take away from Tim."
The American took a short break from the game following Gullikson's death.
"Sure it was tough when he passed away," Sampras said.
"I didn't want to play tennis, but time heals things and this is a great start to win here and I certainly hope everyone stays healthy around me.
"Tennis is a great game and you love to win every match you play, but ultimately it's not the most important thing in life -- that's your health.
"It really woke me up to some things that I have never really had to deal with before. You live every day like it means something.
"He will always be in my mind when I play, especially in moments like today, very tough conditions."
Sampras echoed calls by critics for the tournament to be switched to the cooler month of March.
"I would be in favour of that," Sampras said. "A little cooler, I wouldn't mind having more of break in and January and February."
Medical experts and many players criticised the timing of this year's tournament which was hit by heatwave conditions.
"This is the toughest major I think I've won so far, physically...and to come through is a good effort," he said.

Temperatures soared to about 50 degrees Celsius (122 Fahrenheit) courtside over three straight days in the middle of the tournament, prompting organisers to close the roof on Centre Court to screen out the heat.

World number one women's player Steffi Graf needed to be treated for heat exhaustion after her shock fourth-round exit and Romania's Irina Spirlea and Sabine Appelmans of the Netherlands were placed on drips following their matches.
Sampras's Open campaign very nearly ended in the fourth round against little known Slovakian Dominik Hrbaty who took the top seed to five sets.
"The combination of that (heat) and the court, it just makes it that much hotter...I don't think I've ever played in conditions like I did in that fourth-round match," said Sampras.
